analysis.summary_en: This study investigated whether microspatial ecological variation in Puerto Rico shapes the insect-specific virome (ISV) of Aedes aegypti and influences dengue virus transmission risk. These results imply that monitoring ISV profiles could inform local dengue risk assessment and vector control strategies, particularly in urban settings.

title: Climate Variability and Dengue Dynamics: A Path Analysis in Surabaya, Indonesia

analysis.research_question_and_background: Dengue fever is a climate-sensitive vector-borne disease, and while associations with climate variables are documented, conventional regression approaches fail to separate direct and indirect climatic pathways, limiting mechanistic understanding and utility for environmental health. This study aims to elucidate the interconnected effects of climatic variability on dengue incidence in Surabaya.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective ecological design was used, integrating monthly dengue incidence data from 2020 to 2024 with meteorological variables including rainfall, temperature, humidity, sunlight duration, and wind speed in Surabaya, Indonesia.
analysis.methods: Seasonal time-series decomposition was applied to characterize temporal dynamics, followed by path analysis within a structural equation modeling framework to quantify direct and indirect climatic effects on dengue incidence.
analysis.main_results: Maximum temperature, relative humidity, sunlight duration, and minimum wind speed exerted significant direct effects on dengue incidence (p < 0.05), while rainfall showed no direct association but acted as a key upstream driver influencing other climatic variables. The structural model explained 52.1% of the variance in dengue incidence.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings demonstrate that dengue dynamics in tropical metropolitan environments are governed by complex climate-mediated pathways rather than isolated climatic predictors. This study provides novel environmental epidemiological evidence to support climate-informed dengue early warning systems and adaptive vector control strategies.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results highlight the need for integrated surveillance systems that incorporate multiple climate variables to predict dengue outbreaks more accurately in urban tropical settings.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its ecological design, which precludes causal inference and may be subject to unmeasured confounding. The evidence strength is moderate due to reliance on retrospective data and a single-city setting.

analysis.summary_en: This study in Surabaya, Indonesia, used a retrospective ecological design with monthly dengue incidence data from 2020 to 2024 and meteorological variables to investigate climate-dengue relationships. The structural model explained 52.1% of the variance in dengue incidence. The findings suggest that dengue dynamics in tropical metropolitan areas are shaped by complex, interconnected climate-mediated pathways rather than isolated predictors, supporting the development of climate-informed early warning systems and adaptive vector control strategies.

title: Integrated surveillance of arboviruses in febrile patients from the Brazilian Amazon reveals complex co-circulation dynamics and hidden viral diversity

analysis.research_question_and_background: Arboviral infections pose a persistent public health burden in the Brazilian Amazon due to overlapping clinical presentations, limited diagnostic capacity, and co-circulation of multiple viruses. The study addressed the need to characterize arboviral infections in febrile patients in Manaus, Brazil, where diagnostic challenges hinder accurate identification.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional study was conducted from February 2021 to February 2023 at a tertiary reference center in Manaus, Brazil. Patients aged 5 years or older with rash and either fever or a history of fever lasting less than 7 days, and a negative thick blood smear for malaria, were enrolled.

Positive samples underwent amplicon-based genome sequencing for phylogenetic analysis, while a subset of RT-qPCR-negative samples was analyzed using de novo shotgun metagenomic sequencing.
analysis.main_results: Among 708 participants, 243 (34.3%) had laboratory-confirmed arboviral infections: 92 (37.9%) DENV, 64 (26.3%) CHIKV, and 4 (1.6%) ZIKV. Coinfections were detected in 83 (34.2%) cases, predominantly DENV+CHIKV (55/83; 66.3%). DENV-1 genotype V and DENV-2 genotypes III (Asian American) and II (Cosmopolitan) were identified. Metagenomic analysis of 35 samples detected Pegivirus hominis and Erythroparvovirus primate 1.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study demonstrates complex co-circulation of arboviruses in Manaus and highlights the utility of integrated surveillance combining molecular, serological, and genomic approaches. analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings underscore the need for integrated diagnostic strategies to improve arbovirus surveillance and patient management in endemic regions. analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its cross-sectional design and single-center setting, which may restrict generalizability. analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study in Manaus, Brazil, enrolled 708 febrile patients with rash to characterize arboviral infections between 2021 and 2023. Using ELISA, RT-qPCR, and metagenomic sequencing, 34.3% of participants tested positive for arboviruses, with dengue (37.9%), chikungunya (26.3%), and Zika (1.6%) predominating. Coinfections were common (34.2%), primarily DENV+CHIKV (66.3%). Phylogenetic analysis identified DENV-1 genotype V and DENV-2 genotypes III and II. Metagenomics revealed Pegivirus hominis and Erythroparvovirus primate 1 in 35 samples. The authors conclude that integrated surveillance combining molecular, serological, and genomic methods is essential to address complex arbovirus co-circulation and hidden viral diversity in endemic settings.
